5553-margery-gred-a-tale-of-old-nurember.title: Margery Gred A Tale Of Old Nuremberg Volume 02
5553-margery-gred-a-tale-of-old-nurember.creator: Georg Ebers
5553-margery-gred-a-tale-of-old-nurember.description: A book by Georg Ebers. But in Autumn the forest is a banqueting-hall where men must say farewell, but with good cheer, in hope of a happy meeting. All that has lived is hasting to the grave. Nevertheless on some fair days everything wears as it were the face of a friend who holds forth a hand at parting.

arxiv-2110-06240.title: Residual Abundances in GALAH DR3: Implications for Nucleosynthesis and Identification of Unique Stellar Populations Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2110-06240.creator: Emily J. Griffith, David H. Weinberg, Sven Buder, Jennifer A. Johnson, James W. Johnson, Fiorenzo Vincenzo
arxiv-2110-06240.description: Abstract We investigate the [X/Mg] abundances of 16 elements for 82,910 Galactic disk stars from GALAH+ DR3. We fit the median trends of low-Ia and high-Ia populations with a two-process model, which describes stellar abundances in terms of a prompt core-collapse and delayed Type-Ia supernova component.

arxiv-2205-02155.title: Effective Mass of α \alpha -Cluster in 12 C Nucleus
arxiv-2205-02155.creator: I. Filikhin, A. Karoui, and B. Vlahovic
arxiv-2205-02155.description: Abstract Based on the effective-mass concept, we perform the Faddeev calculations for a low-lying spectrum of 3 α \alpha states in 12 C nucleus. A three-body potential is used to describe the known breaking of the 3 α \alpha -cluster structure in the nucleus.

arxiv-2303-13068.title: Effects of magnetic field on the evolution of energy density fluctuations
arxiv-2303-13068.creator: Shreyansh S. Dave, Subrata Pal
arxiv-2303-13068.description: Abstract We study the effects of a static and uniform magnetic field on the evolution of energy density fluctuations present in a medium. By numerically solving the relativistic Boltzmann-Vlasov equation within the relaxation time approximation, we explicitly show that magnetic field can affect the characteristics of energy density fluctuations at the timescale the system achieves local thermodynamic equilibrium.

arxiv-2304-08863.title: Remote preparation of optical cat states based on Gaussian entanglement
arxiv-2304-08863.creator: Dongmei Han 1 , Fengxiao Sun 2 , Na Wang 1 , Yu Xiang 2,3 , Meihong Wang 1,3 , Mingsheng Tian 2 , Qiongyi He 1,2,3,∗ , and Xiaolong Su 1,2
arxiv-2304-08863.description: Abstract Remote state preparation enables one to prepare and manipulate quantum state non-locally. As an essential quantum resource, optical cat state is usually prepared locally by subtracting photons from a squeezed vacuum state. For remote quantum information processing, it is essential to prepare and manipulate optical cat states remotely based on Gaussian entanglement, which remains a challenge.

arxiv-2503-01634.title: M-SCAN: A Multistage Framework for Lumbar Spinal Canal Stenosis Grading Using Multi-View Cross Attention
arxiv-2503-01634.creator: Arnesh Batra*, Arush Gumber, Anushk Kumar
arxiv-2503-01634.description: Abstract The increasing prevalence of lumbar spinal canal stenosis has resulted in a surge of MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging), leading to labor-intensive interpretation and significant inter-reader variability, even among expert radiologists. This paper introduces a novel and efficient deep-learning framework that fully automates the grading of lumbar spinal canal stenosis.

arxiv-2508-10598.title: Oops!… They Stole it Again: Attacks on Split Learning
arxiv-2508-10598.creator: Tanveer Khan, Antonis Michalas
arxiv-2508-10598.description: Abstract . Split Learning (SL) is a collaborative learning approach that improves privacy by keeping data on the client-side while sharing only the intermediate output with a server. However, the distributed nature of SL introduces new security challenges, necessitating a comprehensive exploration of potential attacks.

pmc-10538028.title: Association of personality traits with dental visit procrastination by Japanese university students
pmc-10538028.creator: Yukitaka Hoshino, Shota Kataoka, Toshihiro Ansai
pmc-10538028.description: BackgroundProcrastination is a psychological trait that causes individuals to put off doing things that need to be done. It has recently shown to result in the worsening of symptoms due to delays in seeking medical care. However, it is not clear how perception of dental disease influences dental visits.

pmc-10661535.title: Optimizing classroom modularity and combinations to enhance daylighting performance and outdoor platform through ANN acceleration in the post-epidemic era
pmc-10661535.creator: Yubo Liu, Kaifan Chen, Eryu Ni, Qiaoming Deng
pmc-10661535.description: The global COVID-19 pandemic has increased attention to the relationship between the built environment and health, particularly in educational settings where students spend a significant amount of their time. Traditional side daylighting used in schools, while cost-effective and easy to construct, can result in uneven indoor daylighting.

pmc-11401156.title: Perceptions, barriers, and facilitators of cannabis screening during pregnancy and labor: A qualitative study
pmc-11401156.creator: K Skelton, S Nyarko, S Iobst
pmc-11401156.description: BackgroundCannabis is the most commonly used federally illicit substance during pregnancy. Yet, little is known about women’s lived experiences of being screened for cannabis use during pregnancy.ObjectiveTo explore perceptions of cannabis use during pregnancy and childbirth, including experiences of being screened for cannabis use during the intrapartum period.

pmc-11502415.title: IgG4 serologic elevation in a patient with severe hidradenitis suppurativa: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-11502415.creator: Andrew J. Gauger, Mike Fritz, Callie B. Burgin
pmc-11502415.description: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic cutaneous and systemic inflammatory condition. Increasingly, reports have found that immunoglobulins play a role in the exaggerated immune response occurring in severe HS. It is important to recognize these implications as HS patients may present with laboratory abnormalities relating to chronic inflammation and immune activation.

pmc-11561041.title: PONYTA: prioritization of phenotype-related genes from mouse KO events using PU learning on a biological network
pmc-11561041.creator: Jun Hyeong Kim, Bonil Koo, Sun Kim
pmc-11561041.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). MotivationTranscriptome data from gene knock-out (KO) experiments in mice provide crucial insights into the intricate interactions between genotype and phenotype. Differentially expressed gene (DEG) analysis and network propagation (NP) are well-established methods for analysing transcriptome data. To determine genes related to phenotype changes from a KO experiment, we need to choose a cutoff value for the corresponding criterion based on the specific method.

pmc-11692208.title: STATE OF HEALTH AND FUNCTIONAL AGING IN THE IMMIGRANTS AND MIGRANTS IN UKRAINE
pmc-11692208.creator: Olena Tomarevska, Oleksandr Poliakov
pmc-11692208.description: The study of migration factors and the likelihood an impact on aging and health of respondents is important for the healthcare. This study is aimed to evaluate differences in the health of immigrants, migrants, and non-migrants among the 31-105 years. Online study will be perspectives to assess the health state and effectiveness of rehabilitation in migrant’s groups.

pmc-12411558.title: Positive Microbiology in the Movies
pmc-12411558.creator: Manuel Sánchez‐Angulo
pmc-12411558.description: Microbes are essential for sustaining life in our planet. Also, we use microbes for multiple processes like food fermentation, production of antibiotics and other drugs, biofuel production, biomining and so forth. However, this essential role is scarcely represented in commercial movies.

pmc-12568971.title: Circulating vascular biomarkers in relation to physiological indices of aortic stiffness and endothelial function in hypertension
pmc-12568971.creator: Andreas Jekell, Mikael Ekholm, Thomas Kahan, Kristina Lundwall
pmc-12568971.description: Studies investigating the relation between circulating vascular biomarkers reflecting endothelial dysfunction and physiological methods to evaluate vascular function remain limited. We simultaneously evaluated the relation between circulating endothelial biomarkers with physiological non-invasive vascular methods in 107 hypertensive patients with a wide range of mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

pmc-13094826.title: Ecologic Investigative Strategies to Determine Human Plague Exposure Sites, United States, 1991–2018
pmc-13094826.creator: Rebecca J. Eisen, Lynn M. Osikowicz, Erik Foster
pmc-13094826.description: Plague is a rare but potentially life-threatening fleaborne zoonotic disease caused by Yersinia pestis. Public health agencies in the United States use multiple concurrent epidemiologic and ecologic strategies to determine Y. pestis exposure sites. We reviewed 196 plague case files from 1991–2018 to describe effort and yield of implemented strategies.

pmc-13357978.title: Managing complexities of inflammatory rheumatic diseases as a migrant—a qualitative exploration of health literacy experiences
pmc-13357978.creator: Laura Treacy, Lise-Merete Alpers, Sarah Hakim, Maryam Azimi, Heidi A. Zangi
pmc-13357978.description: BackgroundMigrants comprise over 17% of Norway’s population and are at increased risk of limited health literacy, a key determinant of health. Health literacy is shaped by language, culture, social norms, discrimination, and health system responsiveness. Inflammatory rheumatic diseases are complex, chronic conditions requiring long-term, specialised care.

pmc-13557851.title: Synchronous Multifocal Intraductal Tubulopapillary Neoplasm of the Pancreas Treated with Total Pancreatectomy: A Case Report
pmc-13557851.creator: Kohei Suto, Mariko Tsukagoshi, Ayako Yamazaki, Emi Saito, Ryosuke Fukushima, Ryo Muranushi, Kouki Hoshino, Norihiro Ishii, Takamichi Igarashi, Norio Kubo, Kenichiro Araki, Ken Shirabe
pmc-13557851.description: INTRODUCTIONAn intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasm (ITPN) is a rare pancreatic tumor characterized by scant mucin production. Even when associated with an invasive carcinoma component, its prognosis is generally considered more favorable than that of conventional pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. However, its pathogenesis and optimal treatment strategy remain unclear. Herein, we report a case of a synchronous multifocal ITPN treated with total pancreatectomy.

pmc-13674835.title: Endodontic Treatment of Apical Periodontitis Mitigates Systemic Inflammation and Restores the Blood–Brain Barrier Integrity in an In Vitro Model
pmc-13674835.creator: Loredana Bergandi, Mario Alovisi, Elena Tachis, Nicola Scotti, Andrea Baldi, Iris Chiara Salaroglio, Sabrina Digiovanni, Lorena Charrier, Francesca Silvagno, Damiano Pasqualini
pmc-13674835.description: AimA growing body of research supports an association between periapical inflammation and an increased risk of various systemic effects. However, there is currently no scientific evidence demonstrating a causal relationship between this inflammation and changes in epithelial or endothelial permeability in patients with apical periodontitis (AP).
